title: Continuity of a Function
topicTitle: Continuity of a function, types of discontinuity, graphs of discontinuous function
notes: **Definition:** A function $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = a$ if all three conditions hold: (i) $f(a)$ is defined, (ii) $\lim_{x \to a} f(x)$ exists, (iii) $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a)$.
**Informally:** A function is continuous at a point if you can draw its graph through that point without lifting your pencil.
**Continuity on an interval:** $f$ is continuous on $[a, b]$ if it is continuous at every point in $(a, b)$, right-continuous at $a$, and left-continuous at $b$.
**Continuity of standard functions:** All polynomial, rational (where defined), trigonometric (where defined), exponential, and logarithmic functions are continuous on their domains.
**Algebra of continuous functions:** If $f$ and $g$ are continuous at $x = a$, then $f + g$, $f - g$, $f \cdot g$, and $f/g$ (if $g(a) \neq 0$) are all continuous at $x = a$.
**Composition of continuous functions:** If $g$ is continuous at $a$ and $f$ is continuous at $g(a)$, then the composite function $f \circ g$ is continuous at $a$.
**Intermediate Value Theorem:** If $f$ is continuous on $[a, b]$ and $f(a) \neq f(b)$, then $f$ takes every value between $f(a)$ and $f(b)$ at least once on $[a, b]$.
confusion: A function can be continuous at a point but not differentiable there (e.g., $f(x) = |x|$ at $x = 0$). Continuity is a weaker condition than differentiability.
A function can have a limit at a point without being continuous there — the function might be undefined at that point, or its value might differ from the limit.
practice: Determine whether $f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2 & x \neq 1 \\ 3 & x = 1 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 1$.
Find the value of $k$ that makes $f(x) = \begin{cases} kx + 1 & x \leq 2 \\ x^2 & x > 2 \end{cases}$ continuous at $x = 2$.
Use the Intermediate Value Theorem to show that $x^3 - x - 1 = 0$ has a root in $[1, 2]$.
universalFacts: Continuity is essential for the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, which connects derivatives and integrals.
The Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees the existence of solutions to equations but does not tell you how to find them.
